subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A graptolite rhabdosome grows in which direction from the first zooid (sicula), and how is stipe growth described?
options: Upward from the prosicula. Stipe growth is scandent or reclined, never branching
Random and variable. No fixed growth direction exists among the colonial graptoloids
From sicula (first zooid) downward. Stipe growth: scandent (graptoloid) or dendroid
Sideways from the initial bud. Stipe growth is planar and confined to a horizontal sheet
solution: Graptolite: sicula → stipe growth. scandent: stipes merge (Monograptus). Dendroid: branching.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ammonite zonation of sedimentary strata is chiefly used for which purpose?
options: Biostratigraphic dating of Mesozoic rocks
Dating Precambrian banded iron formations
Subdivision of Paleozoic marine successions
Correlation of Cenozoic continental strata
solution: Ammonites: rapid evolution, wide distribution. Excellent index fossils for Jurassic-Cretaceous marine rocks.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A P-wave travels at 6 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 60 km
120 km
20 km
0.3 km
solution: distance = velocity × time = 6×20 = 120 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a complete evaporite sequence, minerals appear from bottom to top in which order?
options: Carbonate → gypsum → halite → potash
Halite → carbonate → gypsum → potash
Potash → halite → gypsum → carbonate
Gypsum → carbonate → halite → potash
solution: Evaporite: decreasing solubility upward. Ca-carbonate first, then Ca-sulfate (gypsum), NaCl (halite), KCl (potash).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What do the inclined layers of cross-bedding reveal about the depositional setting?
options: Randomly oriented, chaotic fabric with no preferred layer orientation
Strictly horizontal layers showing no inclination in any direction
Inclined layers within horizontal strata. Wind or water current direction
Vertically dipping layers formed by folding of originally horizontal strata
solution: Cross-bedding: dune migration. Paleocurrent indicator.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Von Mises stress criterion predicts yielding when:
options: Second deviatoric stress invariant reaches critical value
Maximum principal stress attains the tensile yield strength
Resolved shear stress on the plane equals the cohesive strength
Differential stress drops to zero under hydrostatic pressure
solution: Von Mises: √(J₂) = k. J₂ = second invariant of deviatoric stress. Smooth criterion, good for ductile metals.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which peridotite variety consists of more than 90% of the mineral olivine?
options: >90% olivine. Type of peridotite
Rock with more than ninety percent quartz and minor feldspar
Rock with more than ninety percent pyroxene and no olivine
Rock with more than ninety percent plagioclase feldspar
solution: Dunite: light green, massive. Altered to serpentinite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Pseudosection modeling constructs a thermodynamic phase diagram for which specified condition?
options: ACF diagram projected from quartz and fluid for a fixed bulk composition and a given metamorphic temperature
Petrogenetic grid of univariant reactions independent of bulk composition and valid for any rock type
Thermodynamic phase diagram for specific bulk composition. Perple_X, Theriak-Domino. Isopleths for P-T
AFM diagram valid for one bulk composition and one metamorphic pressure without isopleth contours
solution: Pseudosection: modes + compositions of phases. Contours of T/P. Compare with natural assemblage.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is computed using which two spectral bands of a sensor?
options: Red and Near-Infrared bands
Blue and green visible bands
Thermal and microwave bands
SWIR and TIR wavelength bands
solution: NDVI = (NIR - Red)/(NIR + Red). High = healthy vegetation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Distinguish marine transgression from regression in terms of shoreline shift and the resulting stratal stacking pattern:
options: Both processes move the shoreline progressively landward over time
Transgression: landward shoreline shift (retrogradational). Regression: basinward (progradational)
Regression moves the shoreline landward while transgression moves it basinward, reversing the usual definitions
Transgression moves the shoreline basinward and regression moves it landward
solution: Transgression: sea-level rise + sediment supply < accommodation.Ravinement surface.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral specimen of mass 81 g has a volume of 20 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
solution: SG = mass/volume = 81/20 = 4.05.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Slate is the low-grade metamorphic product of:
options: Basalt (fine-grained volcanic rock)
Shale (mudstone)
Sandstone (cemented quartz grains)
Limestone (calcium carbonate mud)
solution: Fine-grained shale metamorphoses to slate, with characteristic slaty cleavage.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The cleat system in coal refers to which type of naturally occurring fracture set?
options: Random fractures with no preferred orientation and irregular spacing distributed throughout the coal seam body
Joints inclined at high angles to the bedding planes of the coal seam itself
Bedding-plane partings along the depositional surfaces of the original coal seam
Natural fractures perpendicular to bedding. Face cleats (primary) and butt cleats (secondary)
solution: Cleats: orthogonal system. Control permeability. Spacing: mm to m. Face cleats continuous.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Plate boundary triple junctions: RRR type (ridge-ridge-ridge):
options: Two plates converging while the third moves along a transform fault
All three plates converging toward a common central point
All three plates separating. Example: Azores, Afar
One ridge, one trench and one transform fault meeting at a single point
solution: Triple junction: RRR stable (receding). TTT stable (subducting). RRR at Afar: Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Rift.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The principle of isostasy states that the crust is balanced how upon the denser mantle?
options: Crust floats on denser mantle in gravitational equilibrium
The lithosphere remains fixed and rigid over geologic time
Mantle density varies randomly without any relation to relief
Continental crust and oceanic crust have identical densities
solution: Airy: mountain roots. Pratt: lateral density. Glacial rebound confirms.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Conodont elements, which are phosphatic tooth-like structures, are now recognized as belonging to what kind of animal?
options: Arthropod with a mineralised carapace and calcite lens-bearing compound eyes
Mollusk whose aragonitic shell was progressively replaced by phosphate during burial
Annelid worm whose chitinous jaws were secreted as a fused feeding apparatus
Eel-like chordate (Couthovia). Phosphatic tooth-like elements
solution: Conodonts: primitive chordate. Elements used for biostratigraphy. CAI = thermal maturity.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mass extinction events are identified by:
options: Sharp decrease in biodiversity in fossil record
A gradual steady decline spanning several periods
Uniform diversity levels across boundary strata
An abrupt increase in endemism and faunal provinciality
solution: Mass extinction: >75% species loss in <1 Myr. 5 major events identified. Sharp drop in diversity in stratigraphic record.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Heavy minerals concentrated by flowing water in stream beds form a:
options: Placer deposit
Evaporite deposit
Vein deposit
Porphyry deposit
solution: Placers (e.g. of gold, cassiterite) form where moving water sorts dense, durable grains.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In the samarium-neodymium radiometric system, the radioactive parent samarium-147 decays by alpha emission to produce which daughter isotope?
options: Neodymium-143
Neodymium-144
Neodymium-142
Neodymium-145
solution: Sm-Nd dating: 147Sm → 143Nd. Half-life ~106 Ga. Good for mafic/ultramafic rocks. Less affected by metamorphism.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Isograd: line on map connecting points of same metamorphic grade. Defined by:
options: First appearance of index mineral (e.g., garnet, staurolite)
Last appearance of the index mineral in the same metamorphic zone
Boundary between two different rock types on the geological map
Constant abundance of one mineral throughout the metamorphic belt
solution: Isograd: reaction isograd. Garnet-in, staurolite-in, kyanite-in. Maps P-T conditions.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Exsolution lamellae in feldspar indicate:
options: Slow cooling from high temperature
Rapid quenching of a volcanic glass
Late-stage hydrothermal fluid infiltration
Mechanical deformation during mountain building
solution: Exsolution: two feldspar phases separate on cooling. Perthite: K-feldspar + plagioclase lamellae. Indicates slow cooling.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the age, composition, and significance of the Peninsular Gneissic Complex of the Dharwar region?
options: Closepet Granite batholith that intrudes the E-W greenstone belts of Kolar
Cuddapah platform cover that unconformably overlies the older basement rocks
Banded gneissic complex in Dharwar. TTG composition. 3.4-3.0 Ga
Sargur supracrustal rocks that lie folded within the gneissic terrain of Mysore
solution: Peninsular Gneiss: basement for Dharwar. Multiple deformation events. Migmatitic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To extract 15 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/15 = 3 : 1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ophiolite complexes are slices of oceanic lithosphere thrust onto continental margins. An ophiolite sequence consists of which units?
options: Continental lithosphere thrust beneath the oceanic crust forming a thick slab that descends to depths of several hundred kilometres
Volcanic arc crust accreted onto the continental margin during the closure of a back-arc basin
Sediments deposited in a continental rift basin recording progressive transgression
Oceanic lithosphere obducted onto continent. Harzburgite → layered gabbro → sheeted dike → pillow lava → pelagic sediment
solution: Ophiolite: Oman, Troodos (Cyprus). Moho transition zone. SSZ (supra-subduction zone) ophiolite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which minerals are characteristic of the high-pressure, low-temperature blueschist facies?
options: Chlorite, epidote, albite, actinolite (greenschist minerals)
Pyroxene, garnet, feldspar with no hydrous minerals at all
Glaucophane (blue amphibole), lawsonite, jadeite, aragonite
Hornblende, biotite, garnet, staurolite (amphibolite minerals)
solution: Blueschist: HP/LT subduction. Glaucophane: diagnostic blue amphibole. Jadeite: Na-pyroxene.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is shotcrete and how is it applied in underground construction?
options: Concrete cast in timber formwork and cured for twenty-eight days before any loading
Precast panels bolted onto the rock face with no bonding material at all
Sprayed concrete (dry or wet mix). Steel fiber reinforced. Applied to rock surface
Poured tremie concrete placed underwater through a tremie delivery pipe
solution: Shotcrete: immediate support. Add accelerator. Wire mesh or fiber. 50-100mm thick.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Packer tests in boreholes are used to isolate and measure the permeability of:
options: Specific depth intervals in borehole for permeability measurement
The entire borehole so that the full saturated aquifer thickness is tested
Surface water bodies from the influence of the borehole test
Only the aquitard layers that bound the main aquifer under test
solution: Packer test: inflatable packers seal interval. Pump or slug test in isolated zone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Crystal twinning: contact twin vs penetration twin:
options: No difference. Contact and penetration twins are simply two names for the same intergrowth
Contact = interpenetrating. The two types share identical geometry at the junction
Contact: shared plane (mirror). Penetration: shared point (interpenetrating)
Same thing. Both twins form by the same interpenetrating growth mechanism
solution: Contact: staurolite, gypsum. Penetration: fluorite, pyrite, garnet twins.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral has passed through 2 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 1.3 (in the given time units). Its age is:
solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 2×1.3 = 2.6.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the chemical composition of dolomite, and how does it typically form?
options: CaCO3 — the same as calcite, forming inorganically from seawater
CaMg(CO3)2 — forms by Mg replacement of calcite
FeCO3 — iron carbonate formed under reducing diagenetic conditions
SiO2 — silica mineral formed by recrystallization of biogenic ooze
solution: Dolomite: effervesces weakly in cold HCl. CaMg(CO3)2.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What geological setting gives rise to a mud volcano erupting mud and gas?
options: A normal volcanic eruption of molten lava and pyroclastic material rising from the deep mantle of the earth
Ejection of mud and gas from depth. Overpressured sediments. Often in accretionary wedges
An ordinary cold spring discharging mineral-poor surface water near the coast
A fault scarp formed purely by tectonic extension of the earth's crust at the surface
solution: Mud volcano: methane, water, fine sediment. Onshore (Azerbaijan) and offshore. Cone-shaped.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which vegetation index performs better in high-biomass areas and incorporates blue along with red and near-infrared bands?
options: A simple two-band ratio of red and near-infrared reflectance values, identical to NDVI
Identical to NDVI but with atmospheric correction applied and no soil adjustment factor as well
Enhanced Vegetation Index. EVI = 2.5×(NIR-R)/(NIR+6R-7.5B+1). Better for high biomass
An index that requires no soil brightness adjustment factor in its calculation
solution: EVI: reduces atmospheric and soil noise. For dense vegetation (Amazon). MODIS EVI product.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes sapping or spring erosion and the valley forms it produces?
options: Groundwater outflow → headward erosion. Box canyon, amphitheater valleys. Colorado Plateau
Erosion caused only by the overland flow of surface water during periods of heavy rainfall in the region
Erosion caused only by the action of wind on the land surface of the surrounding arid desert region of the world today
Erosion caused only by the action of moving glacier ice over the land surface lying below the glacier
solution: Sapping: chemical weathering at spring outlets. Canyon head propagation. Piping erosion.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes isostasy and distinguishes the Airy and Pratt models of crustal equilibrium?
options: Isostasy involves only lateral variations in the density of the Earth's crustal rocks and nothing else at all whatsoever
Buoyant equilibrium of Earth's crust. Airy (variable root depth) vs Pratt (variable density)
Isostasy involves only lateral variations in the thickness of the Earth's crust and nothing else whatsoever
The Earth's crust is not in any kind of equilibrium at all in any region of the world today
solution: Airy: mountains have deep roots (like iceberg). Pratt: density varies laterally. Flexural isostasy.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes the surface produced when ice-rich permafrost thaws?
options: Irregular surface from thawing of ice-rich permafrost. Subsidence, ponds
Landforms produced by wind erosion in arid desert regions of the world
Landforms carved by the erosion of moving glacier ice over the bedrock below
Landforms built by the deposition of river-borne sediment in the floodplain of a river
solution: Thermokarst: alases (depressions), baydzherakhs (soil pedestals). Climate warming.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes piping, the conditions that promote it, and its consequence in wind-deposited silt?
options: Uniform removal of a thin layer of soil by unchannelled surface water flow during heavy rainfall
Erosion of deep channels in the surface of the soil by running water during flood events
Removal of material across the surface of the ground by flowing water at the surface of the land during heavy storms
Subsurface erosion (tunnel erosion) in wind-deposited silt. Vertical permeability → collapse
solution: Loess: metastable structure. Piping: rapid erosion along preferential flow paths.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which option correctly describes a barrier island, its lagoon and the inlets that cut through it?
options: Island of resistant bedrock rising steeply above the sea surface offshore from the coast
Island built by volcanic eruptions on the sea floor near the coastline of the mainland
Long, narrow sand island parallel to coast. Lagoon behind. Inlet cuts
Sand ridge attached to the mainland coast at one of its two ends
solution: Barrier: wave-dominated. Dune ridge, beach, washover fans. Sea-level rise → barrier transgression.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A functioning GIS needs hardware, software, data, people, and methods, with spatial data stored in which two main forms?
options: The physical computers and the GIS software packages, since the data and the people are not counted as components of a GIS
Only the hardware, software and methods used, without the data and people
Hardware, software, data, people, methods. Spatial data: raster (grid) and vector (points, lines, polygons)
Only the data and the people who manage, update and use the system
solution: GIS: capture, store, analyze, display spatial data. ArcGIS, QGIS.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What engineering problem does phyllite pose due to its smooth cleavage planes?
options: Massive rock with high strength in every direction and no planes
Excellent foundation rock with very high bearing capacity
Ideal aggregate with high resistance to weathering and slaking
Smooth cleavage planes → low friction. Slake-prone
solution: Phyllite: foliated, anisotropic. Weak along cleavage. Weeps along foliation planes.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Isotope ratios: εNd positive = depleted mantle source. εNd negative =:
options: Depleted mantle source that has lost incompatible elements
Primitive undifferentiated mantle of chondritic composition
Source that provides no information about magma provenance
Enriched mantle or continental crustal source
solution: εNd = ((¹⁴³Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd)_sample/(¹⁴⁴Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd)_CHUR - 1) × 10⁴. Positive: depleted. Negative: enriched/crustal.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the nature and tectonic setting of the Closepet Granite batholith in southern India?
options: Early Archean (3.4 Ga) supracrustal belt within the Sargur greenstone sequence
Granite batholith between E and W Dharwar Cratons. ~2.5 Ga. Late Archean
Proterozoic (~1.8 Ga) platform carbonate sequence of the Cuddapah basin
Paleozoic (Permian) coal-bearing rift fill of the Gondwana basins of India
solution: Closepet: N-S trending. High-K, calc-alkaline. Anatectic origin. Mantle+crustal source.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Provenance analysis — heavy mineral assemblage:
options: Ultra-stable (zircon, tourmaline, rutile) vs metastable (garnet, staurolite, kyanite)
Only ultra-stable minerals such as zircon survive, with all others destroyed during transport
Only metastable minerals such as garnet are present, indicating an extremely mature sediment
Only opaque minerals like magnetite and ilmenite are used in provenance determination
solution: ZTR index (zircon-tourmaline-rutile): high = mature, recycled sediment.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A metamorphic facies represents a set of rocks that equilibrated under which controlling condition?
options: P-T conditions: Zeolite, Greenschist, Amphibolite, Granulite, Blueschist, Eclogite
Rock types such as slate, phyllite, schist and gneiss formed in major orogenic belts
Relative geological age of the metamorphic event within the regional metamorphic terrane
The distance of a rock sample from the nearest mapped igneous intrusive body on the surface
solution: Barrovian: greenschist→amphibolite→granulite (increasing T). Blueschist: high P/low T.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 80 km
0.4 km
20 km
160 km
solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×20 = 160 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What distinguishes stratabound ore deposits from stratiform ore deposits?
options: Both terms mean the same thing and are used interchangeably in ore geology
Stratabound ore deposits are always syngenetic with the enclosing sedimentary beds that contain them
Stratabound: confined to specific horizon. Stratiform: bedding-parallel, syngenetic
Stratiform ores are always epigenetic, cutting across the sedimentary bedding
solution: Stratabound: epigenetic but stratigraphically controlled. Stratiform: syngenetic, within bedding.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Sm-Nd dating, based on ¹⁴⁷Sm→¹⁴³Nd decay, suits mafic and ultramafic rocks, and εNd values distinguish what?
options: ¹⁴⁷Sm → ¹⁴³Nd (α). T½ = 106 Ga. For mafic/ultramafic, REE minerals. εNd for mantle vs crust
U-Pb method applied to zircon crystals of the same rock body that is being studied in detail
C-14 method applied to organic remains of the recent deposits and overlying sediments
Rb-Sr method applied to whole rocks of the same igneous suite and its various units
solution: Sm-Nd: immobile during alteration/metamorphism. Model ages (T_DM, T_CHUR). Crustal residence.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How are folds classified by interlimb angle, from gentle through to isoclinal folds?
options: Gentle (>120°), Open (70-120°), Close (30-70°), Tight (<30°), Isoclinal (0°)
Gentle (30-70°), Open (<30°), Close (70-120°), Tight (>120°), Isoclinal (90°)
Gentle (<30°), Open (30-70°), Close (70-120°), Tight (>120°), Isoclinal (180°)
Open (0-30°), Close (30-60°), Tight (60-90°), Isoclinal folds with 90° interlimb angle
solution: Interlimb angle: <30° tight, 0° isoclinal (parallel limbs).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 2 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 3.9 Mt
6 Mt
7.8 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 2×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 7.8 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Groundwater recharge can be estimated by which of the following methods?
options: Only the measurement of the total annual rainfall received by the region concerned during the year
Water table fluctuation, chloride mass balance, baseflow separation, isotope tracers
Only the results of a single pumping test that is carried out on the aquifer under study within the region
Only the pan evaporation data that is collected from the nearby weather station on each day of the year
solution: Recharge: critical for resource assessment. WTF: ΔS = S_y·ΔH. Chloride: P·Cl_p = R·Cl_gw.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What streak colour does the mineral chalcopyrite produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
options: Greenish black
Brassy yellow
Brownish yellow
Dark grey
solution: Chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) — brassy yellow. Most important copper ore mineral.
